title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-19
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CD > EAC > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: A pristine sound‑board recording of a 1970 show that dazzles with an epic Dark Star, soaring St. Stephen and fiery Turn‑On‑Your‑Love‑Light.
ai_review.review: The matrixed SBD source is crystal clear, delivering every nuance of the band’s 1970 performance.  Highlights include a transcendent Dark Star (with its famed 16‑minute “Feeling Groovy” jam), a tight St. Stephen, a thunderous Not Fade Away and an exuberant Lovelight punctuated by Pigpen’s legendary rap.  Overall the set is regarded as one of the era’s finest, with only minor complaints about occasional tape noise.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (over 30) praise both the musical performance and the superb sound‑board quality, yielding a weighted average near 4.6.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, clear, superb SBD/matrix mix; occasional minor hiccups (tiny scratch at 16 min, brief drop‑outs) noted but not detracting.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows from a powerful Dark Star into St. Stephen, then rides through an intense Not Fade Away with multiple jams before closing on an exuberant Lovelight; reviewers cite the pacing and transitions as exceptional.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is repeatedly lauded – “perfect guitar tone,” “feedback squeal,” and “nailing the Feeling Groovy jam.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh gets a brief nod for his bass bomb on Morning Dew; otherwise not heavily mentioned.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir praised for dual‑guitar interplay, lead stretching and “unique tone” during Dark Star and China Cat.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums are noted as “perfect match” to the guitars and a driving force behind the high‑energy jams.
